_note: FOUR HOOKS RUN. The crisis floor, on UserPromptSubmit: every prompt is
pattern-matched for crisis signals, and a hit puts the protocol in front of the
model before it answers - SAF-001, "Safety outranks everything else the system
is doing." It only adds context: it cannot block, write or commit. It
over-triggers by design; a false positive costs one line.
The save, on Stop: data/ is committed and pushed to the branch the session is on
at the end of every turn - DEP-005. A phone session's branch is carried into main
by .github/workflows/merge-sessions.yml. The brief, on SessionStart: brings main
in, and says out loud when a save failed or a session branch never reached main
- DEP-006. The sandbox reminder, also on UserPromptSubmit: in a chat switched on
with /sandbox, every prompt is told to read data/ as data-sandbox/. Every other
hook is off.
The hooks that are written but switched off live in .claude/hooks/parked.json,
each in the shape it takes here and with the reason it exists. Claude Code never
reads that file. Turning one on is a move from it into `hooks` below, under its
own event name.
JSON has no comment syntax, and Claude Code will NOT accept one here: a // or
/* */ comment makes it discard this entire file - permissions and all - exactly
as a missing brace would. Nor is an unknown key inside `hooks` a hiding place:
event names are validated, and a key that is not an event takes the file down
with it. That is what the old hooks["//"] parking bay did.
The code is in .claude/hooks/, and `node .claude/hooks/selftest.mjs` proves each
one still runs and decides, switched on or not.
